scenarios.title: Mumbai inbound delay
scenarios.description: A synthetic carrier notice delays the inbound material shipment by two days. Compare qualified recovery sources and explain the first shortage day.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Tokyo customs clearance delay
scenarios.description: A synthetic customs-clearance hold is modeled as a five-day inbound shipment delay. The cause is a demonstration narrative, not a live customs event.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Beijing component delivery interruption
scenarios.description: A synthetic supplier dispatch interruption delays the shipment by four days. Compare local timing and the related customer-order exposure.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Mumbai extended route disruption
scenarios.description: A synthetic logistics disruption postpones one shipment by nine days. Show why more severe delay can increase uncovered demand; do not infer closure of other routes.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Tokyo short delay
scenarios.description: A one-day synthetic shipment delay tests whether available stock and dated receipts cover demand. Recommend action only if the calculation warrants it.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Beijing no-disruption control
scenarios.description: A zero-delay control case tests that the system does not manufacture a disruption or recommend unnecessary procurement.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Mumbai budget-constrained recovery
scenarios.description: A five-day synthetic delay with a zero additional-spend ceiling. Demonstrate blocked planning and revising constraints instead of inventing an affordable plan.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Tokyo deadline-constrained recovery
scenarios.description: A six-day synthetic delay with recovery required by planning day 2. Show whether qualified supply can meet the deadline and explain infeasibility when it cannot.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Beijing prolonged inbound delay
scenarios.description: An eight-day synthetic inbound delay on a different material and plant. Compare affected orders, qualified sources and INR-normalized purchase estimates.
questions: What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?

scenarios.title: Mumbai conflicting supplier messages
scenarios.description: Two synthetic reports disagree about the same recovery booking arrival. The Investigator must surface the conflict rather than silently choose the newer message.
questions: Explain the supplier messages, conflicts or corrections and their effect on recovery options.
What is at risk, and which evidence supports it?
What should I do next, and what assumptions should I review?
